scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, and deploying an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills would resolve it.

H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation failures starting around August are producing incorrect or estimated bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter read collection or the field-to-billing handoff degraded since August (missed/late/invalid reads), causing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic errors in bill calculation or acceptance of reads, directly causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A shortage of field reading staff/contract headcount since August caused incomplete manual read routes, increasing estimate substitutions and bill disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion for the Aug-Sep 2026 period was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — i.e. roughly 12% of scheduled manual reads were not completed during the dispute-surge window, which would push more accounts into estimate substitution.

Across 2440 dispute tickets, median resolution was 1.6 days and p90 was 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA target — ticket response speed is not degraded, so the surge is driven by ticket volume/content (likely bill accuracy), not by slow handling.
billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records for the review window, meaning no tariff rate changes occurred that could explain the wrong bills behind the dispute surge.

billing-db shows 1240 disputed bills had an ESTIMATED read and 1785 had an ACTUAL read (3025 total): a clear majority (59%) of disputes involve bills based on actual meter reads, not estimate substitution. This means estimate-substitution-driven causes (AMI/MDMS failures, field read degradation, staffing) can at most explain the minority (41%) of the dispute volume, pointing toward a billing calculation/import issue affecting even bills with accepted actual reads.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortage of three meter readers since July causes late routes, pushing those accounts to estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim (NON_AUTHORITATIVE), not evidence, and SH-FIELD has a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward staffing attribution.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year corroborates the existing authoritative evidence E-03 (billing-db tariff change log, 0 records), reinforcing that tariff changes are not a cause of the dispute surge. As an unverified stakeholder claim it adds no new weight beyond what E-03 already establishes.

crm-tickets monthly dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 jumping to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming the timing of the surge (roughly doubling starting August) but saying nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (E-08) is a policy document confirming that route priority changes are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, matching the existing K-DISPATCH constraint; it bears on governance/authority for the push_route_update protected action, not on the causal question of what is producing wrong bills.
